title: CircuitPython data types
text:
Core built-in data types
In CircuitPython, data types are mostly the same as Python, but with important constraints due to limited memory and performance on microcontrollers.
Below is a complete, practical overview of CircuitPython data types, with notes on when and why to use each.

title: CircuitPython data types
text:
NoneType
x = None


Represents “no value”
Common for defaults or placeholders



Boolean (bool)
True, False

Used for logic and conditions
Very small memory footprint



Integers (int)
x = 42

Arbitrary precision in theory
In practice: limited by available RAM
Much cheaper than floats

📌 Use ints whenever possible


Floating Point (float)
x = 3.14

32-bit floats (single precision)
Slower and more memory-hungry
Avoid in tight loops if possible

title: CircuitPython data types
text:
Text & Binary Data

Strings (str)
s = "hello"

UTF-8 strings
Immutable (cannot be changed in place)
Repeated concatenation causes fragmentation

📌 Prefer building strings carefully or using buffers


Bytes (bytes)
b = b"ABC"

Immutable sequence of bytes
Efficient for binary data
Common in I/O and communication



Bytearray (bytearray)
buf = bytearray(10)

Mutable sequence of bytes
Very memory-efficient
Excellent for buffers, sensors, displays

⭐ Highly recommended for performance

title: CircuitPython data types
text:
Collections

Tuple (tuple)
t = (1, 2, 3)

Immutable
Lower overhead than lists
Good for constants



List (list)
lst = [1, 2, 3]

Mutable
Higher memory overhead
Avoid large or frequently resized lists



Dictionary (dict)
d = {"a": 1, "b": 2}

High memory cost
Slower than lists/tuples
Use sparingly on microcontrollers



Set (set)
s = {1, 2, 3}

Supported, but expensive in memory
Rarely used in CircuitPython projects

title: CircuitPython data types
text:
Special & Advanced Types

Range (range)
for i in range(10):

Memory-efficient
Does not create a list
Always prefer over list(range())



Memoryview (memoryview)
mv = memoryview(buf)

Zero-copy view of buffers
Extremely efficient
Ideal for slicing bytearrays

⭐ Advanced but very powerful


Function (function)
def foo():
    pass

First-class objects
Minimal overhead



Class / Object (object)
class Foo:
    pass

Supported
Each instance uses memory
Avoid heavy OOP patterns

title: CircuitPython data types
text:
Not Available or Limited



Type
Status




complex
❌ Not supported


decimal
❌ Not supported


fractions
❌ Not supported


numpy
❌ Not available


Large recursion
⚠️ Limited stack

title: CircuitPython data types
text:
Performance & Memory Guidance (Very Important)
Best choices for microcontrollers
✔ int
✔ bool
✔ tuple
✔ range
✔ bytearray
✔ memoryview
Use sparingly
⚠️ float
⚠️ list
⚠️ dict
⚠️ set
⚠️ str concatenation
In summary, CircuitPython supports most core Python data types, but memory-efficient types like int, bytearray, and range are strongly preferred.

text:
VS Code
Visual Studio Code (VS Code) is a free, lightweight, and highly popular source-code editor developed by Microsoft. It’s designed for programmers to write, debug, and manage code efficiently across many languages.

Key Features

Multi-Language Support
Works with Python, JavaScript, C++, Java, Go, Rust, HTML/CSS, and many more.
Syntax highlighting and code completion for each language.


Extensions & Marketplace
Thousands of extensions to add new languages, tools, and themes.
Examples: Python, GitHub Copilot, Prettier, ESLint.


Integrated Terminal
You can run commands directly in the editor.
Supports PowerShell, Command Prompt, bash, and others.


Debugging
Built-in debugger for many languages.
Can set breakpoints, inspect variables, and step through code.


Git & Version Control
Native integration with Git.
Commit, push, pull, and view changes without leaving the editor.


IntelliSense
Smart code suggestions, autocompletion, and parameter hints.
Helps you write code faster and reduce errors.


Cross-Platform
Runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.



Installation
Follow this link and download appropriate installer for your platform:
https://code.visualstudio.com/

title: Setting up your board
text:
CircuitPython extension for VS Code

Key Features

Syntax Highlighting

Highlights CircuitPython code (Python 3 syntax plus Adafruit-specific modules like board, digitalio, neopixel).



Snippets
Provides quick code snippets for common tasks:

Controlling LEDs
Reading sensors
Using I2C/SPI devices
NeoPixel strips



Library Awareness
Helps you see which CircuitPython libraries are used and suggests installing them into your lib folder.


Code Navigation
Jump to definitions and auto-complete for CircuitPython modules.
Integration with USB Drive
Works well when your board appears as CIRCUITPY:

Quickly copy code.py to the board
Recognizes the board type and version

Helpful Documentation

Provides inline help for Adafruit modules.




Installation and use
This guide explains how to install and use the CircuitPython extension for VS Code:
https://learn.adafruit.com/using-the-circuitpython-extension-for-visual-studio-code/overview

title: Testing your board
text:
Flash onboard LED
https://github.com/WaylandM/Biomaker-CircuitPython/blob/main/examples/flash_onboard_led/code.py
This program wil
import time
import board
import digitalio

led = digitalio.DigitalInOut(board.LED)
led.direction = digitalio.Direction.OUTPUT

while True:
    led.value = True   # LED on
    time.sleep(0.5)
    led.value = False  # LED off
    time.sleep(0.5)
